title: EXP-112 - Hello World Part 7 Section 9: FlexLayoutHome in FlexLayoutMain's homepage Region of FX_CustomerPortal (Type VerticalBox; Regions header, spacer, grid, spacer2, buttons), with the EXP-111 Carried Readbacks in the Gate and a Close/Reopen Readback
objective: Build Hello World Part 7 Section 9 (15:24-16:54) on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope): a nested FlexLayout FlexLayoutHome in FlexLayoutMain > Region03: homepage with Type VerticalBox and five regions: header (4 FormUnit, Horizontal, Middle, Center), spacer (1 FormUnit), grid (2 Flex, Fill), spacer2 (1 FormUnit) and buttons (1 Flex, Fill). T1 is a read-only gate that also reads back the four EXP-111 values not confirmed as text. T2 places and names FlexLayoutHome (one Save). T3 sets Type VerticalBox and the header and spacer regions (dialog OK, one Save). T4 adds grid, spacer2 and buttons (dialog OK, one Save). T5 verifies everything after an ordinary close and reopen and writes the final audit. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt7.md Section 9 (lines 241-255) and transcript lines 492-504 (15:24-16:54), recipes/components/add-component-from-toolbox.md, recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-111, EXP-109 and EXP-105 records. Read nothing else: no other records and no Part 7 Section 10 or later. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-112-hello-world-part-7-section-9-flexlayouthome.md and evidence/EXP-112/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109 lesson): if a task cannot finish all its components, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T5; if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log.

Designer gate (T1, read-only except at most one reopen): User scope; FX_CustomerPortal open and clean (Save disabled), no dialog open; if it is not open, open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record the Components tree under FlexLayoutMain: Region00: menu (ButtonSignIn, ButtonHome, ButtonCart), Region01: spacer1, Region02: signinpage (StaticSignIn, StaticImage1, StaticCustID2, EditCustID, ButtonSignIn2, in this order), Region03: homepage, Region04: cartpage, Region05: spacer2 (header and footer components unchanged; the footer's Region00: UNKNOWN0 noted as already present). Expected: no component under Region03: homepage. If any component is already there, or the other regions differ, record it and stop blocked. Record the baseline console error count and one screenshot of the tree and canvas.

Carried readback (T1, read-only, from EXP-111): select each component by its Components row (selection only) and read the values below from a screenshot of the Properties panel, because these combobox values are not exposed as accessibility text (EXP-111 T12); expand a collapsed group by a view-only double-click on its label if needed. ButtonSignIn2: Caption FX_sSignIn and Theme Class FX_BlueButton. EditCustID: Justification Center and Binding Type None (Data Source group). StaticCustID2: No Colon True (Miscellaneous > Specific Attributes). StaticImage1: Bitmap File Name; record the text as displayed (EXP-111 saw 'FX_CustomerSignI...', truncated by the column width); a truncated value starting FX_CustomerSignI is sufficient, because FX_CustomerSignIn.png is the only library image with that prefix (EXP-101); do not resize, hover or open the list to read more. Record each value; a value that differs from the expected one is recorded as a finding and does not stop the run (no repair in this run). Screenshots: at most one per component.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task.

Placement (T2, EXP-105 and EXP-108 method): click the FlexLayout row in the Toolbox once, then click once inside the homepage column on the canvas (Region03: homepage, between the signinpage and cartpage columns; away from dividers and adorner icons); record the Components tree: the new FlexLayout (expected flexLayout1_USER or similar) must be the only child of FlexLayoutMain > Region03: homepage, with one auto region Region00: UNKNOWN0. A FlexLayout in any other region gets the toolbar Undo once and the run stops blocked. Never drag. Record its defaults (Name, Size, Flex Attributes; expected Index 3 Target homepage) and whether it fills the region (the homepage region is Orientation Fill). Name: plain fill FlexLayoutHome and Tab; verify the Name in the Components tree (the Properties header label lags after a rename, EXP-105). Record the console error count after each action. Then exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Screenshots: placement with the tree; the Save response.

Dialog rules (EXP-103-R3, EXP-105, EXP-109): select FlexLayoutHome by its Components row, then open its Edit FlexLayout Attributes through its canvas adorner (identify the control by the tooltip 'Edit FlexLayout Attributes' or its flexlayouteditadorner DOM id, not by position; a coordinate click is allowed only when no reference exists). The dialog must show Type, Auto Size and a Regions grid; if it shows only Region Index and Margin, it is a component's dialog: Cancel and stop blocked. Select a region row before editing it. ID, Length, Minimum/Maximum Length and Default Margin are text editors (plain fill, Tab); Type, Unit, Orientation, Alignment and Pack are lists (open the list, click the option; record the value). Set Unit and Orientation before Alignment and Pack, because rows appear and disappear with them (Fill hides Alignment and Pack; FormUnit hides Minimum and Maximum Length; for Horizontal, Alignment offers Top, Middle, Stretch and Pack offers Start, Center, End). New regions from the Regions add (+) button get defaults (UNKNOWN<n>_USER, 1 Flex, Horizontal, Top, Start). Click the add button once at a time and check the grid after each click; a click that adds no row or more than one ends the task: Cancel and stop blocked. If a planned option does not exist, record the available options, Cancel once (discarding the dialog's changes) and stop blocked; never pick a substitute. At most one correction per field. Keep every existing region in place (no region deletions, no reordering) and never change Auto Size, Region Index or the dialog's own Margin. Record every edited region's values as displayed and the Regions grid before OK; OK once (record any message), then exactly one Designer Save with its response and the Save state. A blocker inside the open dialog ends with Cancel, never with an open dialog across tasks.

Type, header and spacer (T3): open the dialog once and record its starting state (expected Type HorizontalBox, Auto Size False, one region index 0 UNKNOWN0, 1 Flex, Horizontal, Top, Start; if it differs, record it, Cancel and stop blocked). Set Type VerticalBox. Index 0: ID header, Length 4, Unit FormUnit, Orientation Horizontal, Alignment Middle, Pack Center. Click the add button once (two rows); index 1: ID spacer, Length 1, Unit FormUnit, other values left at their defaults. OK, one Designer Save. Screenshots: the dialog at open; the Regions grid and the header region before OK; the Save response.

grid, spacer2 and buttons (T4): open the dialog once and record its state (expected Type VerticalBox, header and spacer as set in T3; if it differs, record it, Cancel and stop blocked). Click the add button three times, one at a time (five rows). Index 2: ID grid, Length 2, Unit Flex, Orientation Fill. Index 3: ID spacer2, Length 1, Unit FormUnit, other values left at their defaults. Index 4: ID buttons, Length 1, Unit Flex, Orientation Fill. OK, one Designer Save. Screenshots: the Regions grid with five rows before OK; the Save response.

Readback and audit (T5, one task): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, record the Components tree (FlexLayoutHome under Region03: homepage with Region00: header, Region01: spacer, Region02: grid, Region03: spacer2, Region04: buttons; everything else unchanged), select FlexLayoutHome by its Components row, open its Edit FlexLayout Attributes read-only and record Type and every region's ID, Length, Unit, Orientation, Alignment and Pack (open no list; Cancel once). Record what the canvas shows in the homepage column (region dividers). Leave the Form open and clean. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state. Screenshots: the reopened canvas with the tree, and the Regions grid.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references. Coordinates are allowed only for the one FlexLayoutHome canvas placement click (T2) and for FlexLayoutHome's Edit FlexLayout Attributes adorner when no reference exists (T3, T4, T5); record each such click. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.
